## Hinge question · Which statement is correct? {#ss1-hinge .sequence-hinge}

```{=html}
<div data-module="hinge" data-correct="3" class="hinge numeric-choices">
<p class="hinge-question">A finite sequence is defined by<br><span data-math="a_n=n^2-4,\qquad n=1,2,3,4,5.">aₙ = n² − 4, n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.</span></p>
<div class="hinge-toolbar"><div class="time" role="timer" aria-label="Time remaining">1:00</div><div class="toolbar"><label>Seconds <select class="timer-duration" aria-label="Question duration"><option>30</option><option>45</option><option selected>60</option><option>90</option><option>120</option></select></label><button class="timer-start primary">Start</button><button class="reset-question">Reset</button></div></div>
<div class="choices">
<button class="choice" data-answer="1" aria-pressed="false"><b>1</b><span data-math="a_3=3">a₃ = 3</span></button>
<button class="choice" data-answer="2" aria-pressed="false"><b>2</b><span>The sequence has no negative terms because <span data-math="n">n</span> is positive.</span></button>
<button class="choice" data-answer="3" aria-pressed="false"><b>3</b><span>12 is the fourth term.</span></button>
<button class="choice" data-answer="4" aria-pressed="false"><b>4</b><span>32 is the sixth term of this sequence.</span></button>
</div>
<div class="hinge-bottom"><p>Fist on chest. Think quietly.<br>On “show”, hold up 1–4 fingers.</p><button class="reveal-answer primary">Reveal answer</button></div>
<div class="hinge-explanation" hidden><strong>3.</strong> <span data-math="a_4=4^2-4=12">a₄ = 4² − 4 = 12</span>.<br>Check both the rule and the allowed indices.</div>
</div>
```

::: notes
Default 60 seconds. Students begin with a fist on their chest, think independently, then show 1–4 fingers together on your verbal cue. Timer expiry does not reveal the answer. The four numbered choices correspond to A–D respectively in the approved plan; correct answer 3 is the planned option C.

- **1:** Confuses position with value. a_3=5, not 3.
- **2:** Transfers the positive-integer restriction on indices to term values. a_1=−3.
- **3 (correct):** a_4=12, and 4 is an allowed index.
- **4:** Extends the formula beyond the defined domain. This sequence ends at n=5; a_6 is undefined here.

Ready: ask why option 4 is tempting, then move to Example 1.3.
Divided: pairs justify choices, then re-poll before revealing.
Reteach: build the table n=1,2,3,4,5 and a_n=−3,0,5,12,21. Recheck both the rule and the domain.
:::
